title: Inverse restrictions for mutually inverse dominant rational maps
statement: Let $X,Y$ be integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $f:U_f\to Y$ and $g:U_g\to X$ be dominant (dense-image) morphisms on dense open subsets. Suppose the composite partial map $g f$ agrees with the identity on some dense open of $X$, and $f g$ agrees with the identity on some dense open of $Y$. There exist dense opens $U\subseteq U_f$ and $V\subseteq Y$ with mutually inverse morphisms $f\prime:U\to V$, $g\prime:V\to U$, such that $f\prime$ followed by $V\hookrightarrow Y$ is the restriction of $f$.

proof.text: Choose dense opens A and B witnessing the two composite equivalences. Factor f restricted to A through U_g and g restricted to B through U_f. Their compositions with g and f are the inclusions of A and B, respectively.

Set U=A intersect f^{-1}(B) and V=B intersect g^{-1}(U), with inverse images interpreted in the original domains. Dominance and irreducibility imply both are nonempty and thus dense. The identities on A and B imply f(U) is contained in V and g(V) is contained in U.

Lift through the open inclusions to obtain U to V and V to U. Compose with their inclusions into X and Y. The identities on A and B give both inverse identities; cancel the monomorphism open inclusions. The forward compatibility equation is the lift factorization equation.

proof_origin.note: Explicit inverse-map restriction argument adapted from the cited proofs; implemented in Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_inverse_restrictions_of_comp_equiv_id
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y]
    (f : X.PartialMap Y) [IsDominant f.hom]
    (g : Y.PartialMap X) [IsDominant g.hom]
    (hf : (f.comp g).equiv (PartialMap.id X))
    (hg : (g.comp f).equiv (PartialMap.id Y)) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_ : Dense (U : Set X)) (hUf : U ≤ f.domain)
      (V : Y.Opens) (_ : Dense (V : Set Y))
      (f' : U.toScheme ⟶ V.toScheme) (g' : V.toScheme ⟶ U.toScheme),
      f' ≫ g' = 𝟙 _ ∧ g' ≫ f' = 𝟙 _ ∧
        f' ≫ V.ι = X.homOfLE hUf ≫ f.hom
